Where it began

Simon Harmer was born in Pretoria on 10 February 1989 and went to Pretoria Boys High School. A right-arm off-spinner who could also bat in the lower order, he began his first-class career with Warriors in the 2010–2011 season and made a lively start. On debut against the Cape Cobras he took 5 for 98 in the first innings and scored 46 and 69. In 2011–12, his first full season, he was Warriors' leading wicket-taker with 44.

The player

His Test debut came against the West Indies at Newlands on 2 January 2015. His first wicket was Devon Smith, bowled in the last over before lunch on the opening day, and he finished the innings with 3 for 71. Then came a long wait. It was six and a half years before he played another Test, against Bangladesh in April 2022, when he and Keshav Maharaj shared 13 wickets in a 2–0 series win.

His finest hour came in India in November 2025. He was Player of the Match in the first Test with 4 for 30 and 4 for 21, took six more wickets in the second, and was named Player of the Series with 17 as South Africa won 2–0, their first series win in India for 25 years. In October 2026, against Australia at Newlands, he took ten wickets in a Test for the first time. By November 2026 he had played 17 Tests and taken 83 wickets at 23.07, with a best of 6 for 16.

What made him special

Control was the heart of it. In India he relied on drift and accuracy, kept the batters quiet, and outbowled the home spinners on their own pitches. His 27 wickets in four Tests there, at 15 apiece, were the most by any South African in India at the time, one more than Dale Steyn.

He was handy with the bat, too, with 391 Test runs at 20.58 by November 2026. His best was 82, his one Test fifty. A hundred had not come along by then, but plenty of number eights would gladly take those figures.

The Essex years

England gave him a second cricketing home. He joined Essex in 2017 and had a wonderful first summer, taking 9 for 95 in an innings against Middlesex, 14 for 172 in the match, and the wicket that confirmed Essex as county champions. He finished that season with 72 wickets at 19.19. In 2019 he captained Essex to their first T20 Blast title, taking seven wickets on Finals Day, a record for that day at the time. Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2020. Along the way he passed 1,000 first-class wickets, only the fifth South African to do so.

And finally

Off-spinners are said to improve with age, like good cheese. Harmer spent his years away from the Test side bowling long spells in county cricket, and when his second chance came he went a long way towards proving the saying right.
